title: /api/health reports the version actually running
body: /api/health now reports the version the daemon is actually RUNNING. It used to read package metadata off disk on every request, so right after an upgrade it reported the new version while the daemon was still executing the old code -- the one question you ask it after deploying was the one it could never answer. When an upgrade is sitting on disk unadopted, the response now says so separately as installed_version, which is your cue to restart.

title: The /new-tab status strip tells the truth too
body: The /new-tab status strip tells the truth too: its version came from the same on-disk read, and its commit hash ran `git rev-parse HEAD` in whatever directory the daemon was launched from, at request time -- so switching branches under a running daemon changed the commit it claimed while the running code did not change.

title: Live-daemon tests stop eating your upgrade notice
body: This what's-new notice can reach you. Five live-daemon test modules spawned a real daemon without isolating the config dir, so every `make ci` run wrote the marker in your real ~/.config and marked the version already seen -- the notice was consumed before an upgrade ever happened.

title: octowright_status reports the daemon's running version
body: octowright_status() now reports the daemon's running version, and tells you when connected followers are on older code and which action fixes it (their client reconnecting -- a daemon restart cannot).
